topic: Correct the marginal-to-conditional quasi-stayer gap in de Chaisemartin, D'Haultfœuille and Vazquez-Bare's continuous-treatment DiD Theorem 1. For iid two-period data with static potential outcomes, conditional parallel trends, known compact treatment support, a baseline trend m bounded by M and L-Lipschitz, and conditional mean causal movement bounded by K|delta|, define g(d,delta)=E[Delta Y|D1=d,Delta D=delta], nu_P(B)=E[sgn(Delta D)1{D1 in B}], and C_P={u: |u|<=M, Lip(u)<=L, |g(d,delta)-u(d)|<=K|delta| on the observed support}. Prove that the full-observed-law sharp WAOSS set is exactly Theta(P)={(E[sgn(Delta D)Delta Y]-integral u dnu_P)/E|Delta D|:u in C_P}; every u must be attained by a legal full potential-outcome law matching P. Prove compact attained interval geometry, the exact point-identification criterion R(P)=max_C integral u dnu_P-min_C integral u dnu_P=0, recovery of the published formula under conditional zero-support, observable obstacle-envelope compatibility, constant-one clipping stability, certified finite LP approximations, and a uniformly honest outer confidence interval on the fixed beta-Hölder, bounded-density, bounded-outcome finite-rectangle support subclass. Do not claim novelty for common-zero-baseline scalar bounded-slope intervals, already in arXiv:2405.04465v4, or invalidate the source's separate parametric estimate. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: Derived the exact affine lift b=(g(D1,Delta D)-u(D1))/Delta D, Y1^u(t)=Y1, Y2^u(t)=Y2+b(t-D2), which preserves the entire observed law, realizes trend u, and has |b|<=K. Derived obstacle clipping with exact constant-one Hausdorff error and checked finite Theta=[-3/5,1] and continuous-density Theta=[-4/7,4/7] witnesses; signed cancellation, equality constraints, empty classes, support versions, denominator boundaries, and the common-baseline prior-art collision were checked. The lift also explains why marginal quasi-stayers alone cannot identify a baseline-specific trend: observed increments constrain u only through support-local cones, while the signed baseline measure transmits unresolved components directly into WAOSS endpoints. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Complete the uniform band-to-finite-program lemma on every allowed rectangle union, including boundary-aware regression coverage, signed-DKW control, measurable endpoint construction, and the stated ratio error. EARLY KILL TEST: Prove that lemma first on a fixed rectangle union with touching boundaries and one component separated from zero changes; if it needs extra density smoothness, strict feasibility, or stronger support assumptions than K4, pivot. STRONGEST-FORM DRAFT (unverified, gaps listed inside): <repo-root>/internal/presolve_drafts/panel_waoss_conditional_completion_frontier.md.

open_problems.why_unsolved: The source theorem recovers the baseline trend through a conditional limit that marginal quasi-stayer mass does not justify. Existing in-repo completion work established only mean-array sharpness using permissive off-arm kernels, while the present claim must preserve the joint observed law and simultaneously enforce static potential outcomes, conditional parallel trends, and the causal-movement bound. The proposed affine lift supplies a candidate construction, but both its legality for every feasible trend and the converse reduction of every legal law to the same support-constrained class remain to be proved.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A two-sided sharpness theorem proving that the identified set equals Theta(P), with an explicit observed-law-preserving full potential-outcome construction for every u in C_P and a converse showing every legal completion induces such a u.

open_problems.why_unsolved: Observed cones induced by different (d,delta) pairs can conflict after imposing the global M bound and L-Lipschitz restriction, especially across touching or disconnected support components, so C_P may be empty even though individual inequalities look feasible. Conversely, conditional support holes need not preclude point identification because the signed measure nu_P may annihilate every unresolved feasible direction. Earlier proposals missed observed-component and endpoint-trace compatibility, while marginal quasi-stayer arguments and common-baseline scalar bounds do not characterize either phenomenon.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A necessary-and-sufficient obstacle-envelope theorem for C_P nonemptiness and a proof that WAOSS is point identified exactly when max over C_P of integral u dnu_P minus min over C_P of integral u dnu_P equals zero, with counterexamples separating marginal quasi-stayers, trend recovery, and target recovery.

open_problems.why_unsolved: Existing econometric LP results either begin with finite support or impose high-level stability on an already finite program. Here the feasible object is a function subject to infinitely many support-local cones and a global Lipschitz restriction. Rectangle-union geometry adds boundary cells, equalities at touching faces, and components separated from zero treatment changes. The missing proof must convert obstacle envelopes into finite constraints while lifting every discretized solution back to a legal continuous function and controlling the signed-measure objective, rather than treating gridding as an implementation heuristic.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: Explicit finite inner and outer LPs whose attained WAOSS intervals converge in Hausdorff distance to Theta(P), with a proved constant-one mesh or clipping bound before division by E|Delta D| and valid treatment of touching and disconnected support components.

open_problems.why_unsolved: Nearby in-repo inference is pointwise and conservative for a fixed finite LP. Uniform WAOSS coverage must instead combine a boundary-aware band for g on rectangle unions, empirical control of the signed baseline measure, deterministic LP discretization error, and estimation of the denominator. These errors must be propagated through two optimized endpoints without stable active sets or strict feasibility, including touching boundaries and components separated from zero changes. Generic regression bands and calibrated projection results each solve only one layer of this composite problem.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: Measurable lower and upper endpoint estimators and an explicit outer interval whose coverage of the entire sharp WAOSS set is asymptotically at least 1-alpha uniformly over the fixed subclass, with a stated ratio error combining regression-band, signed-DKW, mesh, and denominator terms.

open_problems.why_unsolved: On one side of the support frontier, the baseline trend is recovered at a boundary and WAOSS is irregularly point identified; on the other, it is set identified through a Lipschitz envelope. Existing slow-mover theory treats irregular point identification, while standard partial-identification methods hold the set-valued model fixed. Neither supplies one honest procedure or an impossibility boundary across this topology-changing sequence of data-generating processes.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A triangular-array minimax lower bound and an attaining confidence procedure, or a sharp impossibility theorem with an explicit regime statement, as conditional near-zero mass and conditional support distance jointly approach zero.

writing_exemplar.why: Use its motivation around inference failure under varying slow-mover mass, adding the new feature that the causal target changes from point to set identified.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Small treatment changes carry disproportionate identifying content -> their frequency varies across designs -> conventional inference loses uniform validity -> characterize the WAOSS point-to-set transition.

method_exemplars.technique: Separate slow- and regular-mover contributions, trim near-zero denominators, and derive the resulting slower-rate limit law.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Both targets are weighted average slopes whose identifying content concentrates among small within-unit treatment changes.

method_exemplars.technique: Construct bias-robust inference uniform over distributions with differing slow-mover mass.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It provides the closest machinery for distribution-uniform behavior as conditional near-zero mass changes.

method_exemplars.technique: Use the modulus of continuity over a convex Hölder or Lipschitz class to derive honest-CI lower bounds and bias-aware intervals.
method_exemplars.why_closest: WAOSS endpoints are linear functionals of a nuisance constrained to a convex smoothness class, so the transition should admit an analogous modulus characterization.

literature_map:
1. de Chaisemartin, D'Haultfœuille, and Vazquez-Bare (2024, AEA P&P, arXiv:2402.05432) introduce no-stayer WAOSS identification via quasi-stayers and sketch n^(2/5) inference.
2. Their quasi-stayer assumption is marginal, while the proof fixes D1 before invoking near-zero support; this is the precise marginal-to-conditional gap.
3. de Chaisemartin et al. (arXiv:2405.04465v4) derive bounded-slope intervals without quasi-untreated units in the special common-zero-baseline design; that scalar result is prior art, not the present opportunity.
4. de Chaisemartin et al. (arXiv:2201.06898) use exact stayers with the same baseline treatment to identify switcher slopes, underscoring why conditioning on baseline is essential.
5. Callaway, Goodman-Bacon, and Sant'Anna (2024, NBER 32117; arXiv:2107.02637) show that continuous-dose response comparisons need stronger restrictions because dose selection remains.
6. D'Haultfœuille, Hoderlein, and Sasaki (arXiv:2104.14458; Journal of Econometrics) use distributional time restrictions and crossing, not conditional quasi-stayer completion.
7. Graham and Powell (2012, Econometrica) supply the slow-mover and irregular-identification analogy when small within-unit changes carry identifying content.
8. Sasaki and Ura (2025, Econometric Theory, arXiv:2110.12041) develop inference robust to varying slow-mover mass, but not a point-to-set transition.
9. Freyberger and Horowitz (2015, Journal of Econometrics) obtain sharp LP bounds and bootstrap inference for shape-restricted functionals on finite discrete supports, explicitly excluding continuous support.
10. Beresteanu, Molchanov, and Molinari (2011, Econometrica) provide a convex-region and compatible-selection template; Mogstad, Santos, and Torgovitsky (2018, Econometrica) treat weighted functionals under convex shape restrictions.
11. Voronin (2025, arXiv:2503.14940) studies LP-value estimation under multiplicity and shows why uniform conclusions require distributional restrictions.
12. Andrews and Shi (2013, Econometrica) and Kaido, Molinari, and Stoye (2019, Econometrica) provide conditional-moment and calibrated-projection inference frameworks.
13. Belloni et al. (2015, Journal of Econometrics) provide uniform series bands; Cattaneo et al. (2024, Bernoulli, arXiv:2204.10359) provide boundary-adaptive uniform conditional-density machinery.
14. Armstrong and Kolesár (2018, Econometrica, arXiv:1511.06028) give modulus-based honest inference for linear functionals over convex smoothness classes.
15. The live opportunities are full-law sharpness under heterogeneous conditional support, observable compatibility and signed cancellation, certified continuous-support computation, and honest optimized-endpoint inference.
